turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Morning. In you come. What's the problem today?
[SEG0002] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Ag, doctor, it's this spring business again. Sneezing, both eyes itch, and his nose runs the whole time.
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): Sneezing.
[SEG0004] person_1 (DOCTOR): School ok otherwise?
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): Ja.
[SEG0006] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Sorry, hey, parking at the rooms was mad. The robot on the corner was out. Anyway.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): When did it start this spring?
[SEG0008] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Umm. I can't give you a date. After the rains, maybe three weeks, maybe longer, and it's every spring, but I wasn't counting.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): He's on tablets?

[SEG0010] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Allergex. Cetrizine from the chemist. It's ten, ag no, five milligrams, the children's one, by mouth, once a day like the old doctor said. He's eleven now, still on that bottle.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Does he take it every day?
[SEG0012] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Sometimes, not really.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Does it help?
[SEG0014] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Mm, I suppose.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any wheeze?
[SEG0016] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Fever?
[SEG0018] person_3 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sore throat?
[SEG0020] person_2 (CAREGIVER): No.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Anyone else in the family with allergies?
[SEG0022] person_2 (CAREGIVER): His sister. She's allergic to dust. He isn't, not that I've seen.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. Chest is clear, no wheeze. Eyes are pink and the nose is wet and streaming.

[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Could be tree pollen, could be the Highveld grass. I'm not pinning the trigger today, and I won't call it asthma. Working impression is seasonal allergic rhinitis. We'll see what the bloods say before I go further.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Stop the Allergex. For the hay fever, loratadine, 10 milligrams by mouth, one tablet in the morning.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): For the itchy eyes, olopatadine drops, one drop in each eye twice a day.
[SEG0027] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Ok.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): The nurse takes bloods Thursday morning, a pollen IgE panel. No fasting, he can eat breakfast, and give the loratadine after the bloods that morning.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): If those are borderline we do skin-prick testing.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): If the nose does not settle, a sinus x-ray.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll see you in two weeks.
[SEG0032] person_3 (PATIENT): Ok.
[SEG0033] person_2 (CAREGIVER): Thursday morning, ja. I'll bring him through.
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): Good. Off you go.

spec.situation: Sneezing, itchy eyes and runny nose every spring; takes cetirizine 'sometimes'; sister is allergic to dust; no wheeze; doctor changes antihistamine and adds eye drops.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

features: doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.
ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.

omissions.text: Current cetirizine/Allergex use was reported by the caregiver as taken only sometimes/not really every day, and it only helps somewhat ('Mm, I suppose').
The caregiver said the prior cetirizine/Allergex was bought from the chemist and was recommended by the old doctor.
Doctor stated he would not call this asthma.
Doctor stated the trigger was uncertain and could be tree pollen or Highveld grass, and he was not pinning down the trigger today.
Family history detail is recorded incompletely/wrongly: the caregiver said the sister is allergic to dust, and specifically said the patient is not allergic to dust as far as she has seen.
